findings.requirement: NFR-05 (lockout message clause); NFR-07 (announced honest error)
findings.summary: The honest login-lockout message never renders against the real API: the screen matches err.code === 'RATE_LIMITED' but the server's login lockout is code 'LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED'.
findings.detail: src/modules/auth/service.js:318 throws RateLimitError with code OVERRIDDEN to 'LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED' (options spread wins over the class default 'RATE_LIMITED' in src/lib/errors.js:83), the error envelope passes err.code through verbatim (src/middleware/errorHandler.js:28), and the client ApiError carries server codes verbatim (client/src/api/errors.js). Proof re-executed this session: tests/unit/identity.test.js:565 asserts body.error.code === 'LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED' and passed. So on a real lockout, LoginPage's check is false, loginLockoutMessage() (the NFR-05 copy naming the temporary lock and the retryAfterSeconds horizon) is dead code, and messageForAccountError falls through its 'RATE_LIMITED' case to the default branch — the user sees the bare server string 'Too many failed login attempts — try again later' with no retry horizon and no lock-lifts-by-itself explanation. The unit's own test masks the defect by stubbing the WRONG code (LoginPage.test.jsx:181 mocks 'RATE_LIMITED'), which is exactly the class of mistake the FR-10 acceptance correction warns about: the test asserts against a shape the server never produces.
findings.suggestedRepair: In LoginPage (and errorCopy.js), treat the lockout as the family of 429 auth codes — match 'LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED' (and keep 'RATE_LIMITED' for forward-compat), or match err.status === 429 on the login path; update LoginPage.test.jsx to stub the code the backend actually emits ('LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED', pinned by tests/unit/identity.test.js:565).

findings.summary: Same code-mismatch class as AMV-W6-01 on the resend-verification throttle: the client matches 'RATE_LIMITED' but the server emits 'VERIFICATION_RESEND_RATE_LIMITED'.
findings.detail: src/modules/auth/service.js:174 throws the resend throttle with code 'VERIFICATION_RESEND_RATE_LIMITED'. Both resend surfaces check for 'RATE_LIMITED', so the tailored wait-N-then-retry copy (with the formatted retryAfterSeconds horizon) never renders; the fallback shows the server's generic 'Too many verification requests — try again later' without the horizon. SignupPage.test.jsx:172 stubs the wrong code and therefore passes. Lower severity than AMV-W6-01 because the fallback message is still honest and the throttle is not an SRS-numbered clause the way the NFR-05 lockout is.
findings.suggestedRepair: Match 'VERIFICATION_RESEND_RATE_LIMITED' (or err.status === 429) on both resend paths; fix the test stub. Consider centralizing 'is this a 429 throttle' in errorCopy.js so future server code names cannot silently bypass the copy.

findings.summary: STATUS_LABELS lacks the 'processing' status, so a worker-picked-up export renders the raw enum string 'processing' instead of a human label.
findings.detail: db/migrations/0001_core_schema.sql:75 defines data_request_status AS ENUM ('pending','processing','completed','failed') and src/modules/privacy/repo.js:93 transitions requests to 'processing' when the export job is picked up. The `STATUS_LABELS[request.status] || request.status` fallback keeps this honest (never wrong, never blank), and the status-check announcement also speaks the raw word — but it is the only lifecycle state without human copy. Cosmetic; no requirement clause fails.
findings.suggestedRepair: Add processing: 'Processing — the copy is being assembled' to STATUS_LABELS.

findings.summary: The '30 days' in the deletion copy is a static string rather than derived from the 202 response's request.dueAt.
findings.detail: Accurate as shipped: NFR-12's 30-day window is a frozen SRS number and config PRIVACY_ERASURE_DAYS defaults to 30 (src/config/schema.js:128, .env.example pins 30). The dialog necessarily renders BEFORE any response exists, so a static number there is unavoidable; only the post-202 accepted state could render request.dueAt instead. Drift is possible only if a deployment overrides PRIVACY_ERASURE_DAYS away from the SRS's own number. Not a defect against the frozen baseline; recorded so U6R-FIX can decide (rendering dueAt in the accepted state would remove even that drift).

findings.summary: NAME_MISSING is the one reason code never positively rendered by a test — the blocked-user fixture has a fullName, so the test asserts its (correct) absence only.
findings.detail: All five codes share one rendering path (GUIDANCE map + FlagBlock loop) and the NAME_MISSING derivation (missingForReserve: !nonBlank(user.fullName)) mirrors policy.js reasonsFor exactly, so behaviour is verified by inspection and by the four sibling codes' positive assertions. Purely a coverage nicety: a second blocked fixture (or a NAME_MISSING-only fixture) would make the panel's five-code completeness fully machine-checked.
findings.suggestedRepair: Optional: extend the blocked-user test with a fixture missing fullName and assert '(NAME_MISSING)' plus its fix anchor.
